Re: Appeal of denial of total knee replacement  
Member: Taylor Kimura  
Member ID: W381271109  
Procedure: CPT 27447, total knee arthroplasty  
Reference number: POC-972F74519C-71410  
Date of denial notice: August 25, 2026  

Dear Blue Shield of California:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total knee replacement, CPT 27447. The denial states that the imaging findings submitted did not support medical necessity. The submitted records, considered together, establish the radiographic severity and clinical necessity of the requested procedure.

Blue Shield’s published medical policy, BSC7.10, Knee Arthroplasty for Adults, effective December 1, 2025, states:

“Knee arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary when all of the following criteria have been met.”

For degenerative joint disease, the policy requires:

“Documentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management), or documentation of rationale if conservative therapy is considered inappropriate.”

The records satisfy this requirement:

- Progressive knee pain has continued for 14 months and has not been relieved by rest.
- NSAID treatment was attempted for four months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection was administered on June 4, 2026, with only three weeks of partial relief.
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion was completed for 14 weeks, from April 28, 2026, through August 4, 2026, with 18 visits documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

The policy also requires:

“Documentation of limited range of motion, antalgic gait, and pain in knee joint with passive range of motion on physical examination.”

The orthopedic examination documents varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and restricted range of motion from 5 to 100 degrees. The patient also has substantial functional impairment, including inability to climb stairs without assistance and waking three to four times nightly because of knee pain. The clinical records should be reviewed in full, including the examination documentation concerning gait and pain with passive motion.

Most importantly, the policy requires:

“Radiographic evidence of severe osteoarthritis as evidenced by either of the following: i. The presence of definite joint space narrowing with sclerosis and possible deformity of bone ends ii. The presence of large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of the proximal tibia or distal femur.”

The June 25, 2026 weight-bearing knee radiographs demonstrate bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments, lateral joint-space narrowing, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis. These findings document advanced, severe osteoarthritis and directly address the policy’s radiographic requirement. The imaging is not merely suggestive of mild or moderate disease; it shows end-stage joint-space loss in multiple compartments.

The policy identifies osteoarthritis as an eligible underlying condition:

“The reason for the arthroplasty is osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis, osteonecrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint.”

The requested total knee arthroplasty is for severe symptomatic osteoarthritis. The clinical record also documents factors supporting the safety and appropriateness of proceeding: BMI 29, no active infection, no untreated substance use, and nonsmoking status.

Because the imaging demonstrates bone-on-bone disease and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis, and because extensive nonoperative treatment has failed to provide durable relief, I request that Blue Shield overturn the denial and approve CPT 27447.

If Blue Shield continues to deny the request, please provide:

1. The specific version of policy BSC7.10 or any other policy or clinical-review criteria applied to this request;
2. The complete clinical rationale for concluding that the June 25, 2026 radiographs do not demonstrate severe osteoarthritis;
3. Copies of all documents, records, imaging interpretations, and clinical-review materials relied upon in making the determination; and
4. A detailed explanation of which medical-necessity criterion Blue Shield considers unmet.

Please associate this appeal with reference number POC-972F74519C-71410 and confirm receipt. This appeal must be received no later than February 21, 2027.

Sincerely,

Taylor Kimura
